caseno:
Criminal Appeal No. 2339 of 1994 
With
Criminal Appeal No. 2182 of 1994.
lawyer:
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate ----- For Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 2339 of 1994. 
Abdul Quddus, Advocate ----- For Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 2182 of 1994. 
Abdus Salam Mamun, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State.
parties:
Abu Bakker and others ----- Appellant
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
MA Aziz J: These two appeals are directed against the judgment and order date 4-10-94 passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, First Court, Netrokona, in Sessions Case No. 32 of 1993 convicting appellants Abu Bakker, Babul, Md Chand Mia, and Abdul Gafur under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and to pay fine of Taka 1000.00 each, in default to suffer RI for a further period of six months each. 

 4. On completion of investigation police submitted chargesheet against the four appellants and six others under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code. When the case came up for trial, the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, First Court, Netrokona framed charge against all the ten accused persons under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 8. Mr Syed Ziaul Karim, learned Advocate appearing for appellants Abu Bakker, Babul and Md. Chand Mia, submitted that the learned Assistant Sessions Judge erred in law as well as on facts in passing the order of conviction and sentence as there is hardly any credible, corroborative and convincing evidence against the appellants. He submits that the story of recognition of accused Abu Bakker, Gafur and Chand Mia by PW 1 Niranjan Basak in the light of a hurricane suffers from patent infirmity and is unworthy of credit. He further submits that there was inordinate delay in lodging the First Information Report which afforded scope for embellishment of the prosecution case. Mr Ziaul Karim also submits that the confessional statement of co-accused Taheruddin though exculpatory in nature was wrongly used against the appellants as evidence and so was the statement of witnesses recorded by the Investigating Officer under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further submits that PW 4 Osman Ali and PW 6 Abu Siddique did not support PW 1 as regards his disclosure to them of the recognition of accused persons. 

 10. Mr Abdus Salam Mam un, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the state has defended the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence as being properly based on evidence, facts and circumstances of the case. He submits that there is strong evidence of recognition against accused Abu Bakker, Gafur and Chand Mia in the light of hurricane as well as in the focus of torch and the disclosure of such recognition to the witnesses immediately after the occurrence. He further submits that the delay in lodging the First Information Report has been satisfactorily explained and that the trial Court has rightly convicted and sentenced the accused appellant. 

 11.Of the 12 witnesses PW 5 Nurul Islam was tendered. PW 1 is the informant and an eye- witness to the occurrence claiming to have recognised accused Abu Bakker, Gafur and Chand Mia. PW 2 Dipika Rani Basak, wife of PW 1 is also an eye-witness but could not recognise any of the dacoits. PW 3 Sumita Bala Basak, mother of PW 1, is also an eye-witness to the occurrence but could not recognise any of the accused persons. PW 4 Ali Osman and PW 6 Abu Siddique were declared hostile. PW 7 Officer-in-Charge Abul Hashem recorded the First Information Report and was later on examined as PW 12 as the Investigating Officer of the case. PW 8 Md Moksed Ali a neighbour claimed to have been told by PW 1 about the recognition of dacoits. PW 9 Gita Rani Basak is the brother's wife of PW 1 and she heard from PW 1 about the recognition of dacoits. PW 10 Nikhil Chandra Basak is the full brother of PW 1, who heard from PW 1 about the recognition of dacoits and PW 11 Md Abdul Hakim is a neighbor and he heard about the recognition of dacoits from PW 1. 

 13. PW 2 Dipika Rani Basak, wife of PW 1, stated that there was a dacoity in their house on the 19th of Magh, 1398 BS at about 1-30 AM The dacoits were armed with dao, kiris, pipe gun and torch light and they assaulted her husband. There was a hurricane burning in the house. In cross examination PW 2 stated that she could not recognize the dacoits. She also stated that in their room (েকাঠা) there was no hurricane. Her husband disclosed to her about recognition of the dacoits. 

 PW 4 Ali Osman, a neighbor of PW 1, stated that in the following morning of the dacoity PW 1 called him to his house and that neither PW 1 nor his mother PW 3 Sumita Bala Basak stated anything about the recognition of dacoits. He was declared hostile by the prosecution. PW 5 Nurul Islam was tendered by the prosecution. PW 6 Abu Siddique stated that in the night of 19th Magh there was a dacoity in the house of PW 1 and having heard hue and cry he went to the house of PW 1. He further stated that PW 1 did not tell him anything about recognition of dacoits. He was declared hostile by the prosecution. 

 15. PW 7 Abul Hashem was the then Officer-in-Charge of Kendua Police Station. He recorded the First Information Report on the verbal statement of PW 1. In his cross examination PW 7 stated that the First Information Report was lodged 4 days after the occurrence and no medical certificate was submitted in support of the explanation of delay owing to illness of PW 1 or his cousin Sree Jiban Chandra Basak, PW 8 Md Moksed Ali stated that having heard hue and cry he went to the place of occurrence and PW 1 told him about recognition of accused Abu Bakker, Taher, Chand Mia and Bashu in the light of hurricane. In cross examination he stated that one day before the case there was a darbar. 

 18. PW 11 Md Abdul Hakim stated that there was a dacoity in the house of PW 1 on the 19th of Magh two years ago. Having heard hue and cry he went to the Place of Occurrence house and saw the fencing broken. PW 1 disclosed to him about the recognition of dacoits Abu Bakker, Gafur and Chand Mia in the light of hurricane. In cross examination PW 11 stated that after the occurrence there was a darbar in the house of PW 1 but he did not attend. 

 19. PW 12 Inspector of Police Abul Hasem the Investigating Officer in this case (He also deposed as PW 7). On 7-2-93 he was the Officer-in-charge of Kendua Police Station and recorded the First Information Report on the verbal statement of PW 1 Niranjan Chandra Basak. He took up investigation, visited the place of occurrence and recorded the statements of witnesses under section 161 of the CrPC. He arrested accused Taher and forwarded him to the Magistrate for having his confessional statement recorded under section 164 CrPC and a prima facie case having been proved submitted charge sheet under sections 395/397 of the Penal Code. In his cross examination PW 12 stated that the hurricane produced in the court is not broken. He further stated that two hurricanes were mentioned in the charge sheet and that the broken hurricane was given in the jimma of PW 1 (the Informant). 

 20. These are all the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove its case. Now as regards recognition by PW 1 of the appellants, Mr Syed Ziaul Karim argues that besides PW 1 there are 4 other eye-witnesses in the instant case, namely, PWs 2, 3, 9 and 10 who are the wife, mother, brother's wife and the full brother respectively of PW 1 but none of those witnesses could recognise any of the dacoits. Ali of them deposed that PW 1 Niranjan Chandra Basak told them that he recognised accused Abu Bakker, Gafur and Chand Mia in the light of hurricane. PW 1 further stated that in the night of occurrence he was sleeping in the northern room and the hurricane was burning in the southern room. PW 2 stated that there was no hurricane in their room saying" আমাদের কোঠায় কোন হারিকেন ছিল না” Jiban Chandra Basak cousin of PW 1 who claimed to have recognised accused appellant Babul was not examined by the prosecution. Mr Ziaul Karim submits that in the circumstances as above it would be an affront to common sense to ask anyone to believe the story of recognition of the accused appellants by PW 1 inasmuch as there was no hurricane in the room of PW 1. There is considerable force in this argument of Mr Ziaul Karim and we are inclined to accept the contention that the story of recognition is highly doubtful. Furthermore, PW 4 Ali Osman and PW 6 Abu Siddique, who are independent witnesses, stated that PW 1 did not disclose to them about the recognition of the dacoits. 

 21. On the other hand, Mr Abdus Salam Mamun, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, submits that apart from recognition in the light of hurricane PW 1 rccogniscd the accued persons in the focus of torch light used by the dacoits at the time of commission of dacoity. Mr Ziaul Karim submits that recognition of accused persons by torch light or hurricans at the dead of night and under dreadful circumstances is doubtful. Moreover it is highly unusual that the miscreants would focus torch light on their own faces to facilitate recognition inasmuch as it is against the human instinct of self preservation and in support of his contention Mr Karim relied on the decision in the case of Md Musa alias Musaiya @ Shafir Bap vs. Slale reported in 15 BLD 169. It was held in that case that recognition of accused persons by torch light or hurricane light at the dead hours of night and under dreadful circumstances it is ordinarily doubtful unless the witnesses see the miscreants in action from a close proximity. Moreover, it is highly unusual that miscreants would focus torch light in their own faces to facilitiate recognition. 

 From the aforesaid confessional statements it appears that the maker thereof namely, co-accused Taheruddin did not implicate himself with the commission of dacoity. In addition to that there is no other independent evidence connecting the accused appellants to which support may be lent by the exculpatory statement of co-accused Taheruddin. Lastly, Mr Ziaul Karim has drawn our attention to a portion of the judgment at page 111 of the paper book wherein the learned Assistant Sessions Judge referred to and took into consideration the statements of witnesses recorded by the Investigating Officer under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The statement recorded under section 161 CrPC is not evidence. It can only be used to contradict or corroborate the witnesses and hence we hold that the trial Court illegally referred to and considered the statement of witnesses recorded under section 161 of the CrPC. 

 23. The whole case hinges on the recognition of the accused appellants by PW 1 Niranjan Chandra Basak in the light of hurricane and torch which in view of the facts, circumstances and the evidence discussed above appears to be highly improbable and, as such doubtful. In the light of the deposition of PW 1 stating that hurricane was burning in the southern room and he was sleeping in the northern room and in view of the deposition of PW 2 Dipika Rani Basak wife of PW 1 clearly that there was no hurricane in their room (কোঠা) the story of recognition falls through. Furthermore recognition by torch and hurricane at the dead of night being doubtful we hold that the appellants are entitled to get the benefit of doubt and that the appellant should accordingly be found not guilty of the offence charged with and hence the judgment and order of conviction and sentence are liable to be set aside. 

 24. In the result, these two appeals are allowed. The judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, First Court, Netrokona, in Sessions Case No. 32 of 1993 is set aside. The accused appellants Abu Bakker, Babul, Chand Mia and Abdul Gafur are found not guilty of the offence under section 395/397 of the Penal Code and are acquitted accordingly.
